corpusSummary: A 2026 corpus of social-science papers investigates how large language models (LLMs) and generative AI influence research methods, education, health communication, and policy. It highlights methodological uses (coding, framing, multi-agent systems), AI-enabled learning and literacy, health misinformation and AI-driven counseling, and governance, safety, and fairness concerns across diverse contexts and populations.

themes.name: AI as a methodological tool and governance in social science
themes.description: Papers show LLMs supporting coding, content analysis, simulations, and framework-building, while underscoring validation, transparency, and ethical oversight.

themes.name: AI in education and AI literacy
themes.description: Research covers AI's impact on STEM education, learning analytics, teacher practices, and AI literacy across age groups and settings.

themes.name: Health, wellbeing, and information dynamics in AI ecosystems
themes.description: Studies address AI-generated health information, misinformation, patient education, and the psychosocial effects on wellbeing and health behaviors.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, and social dynamics
themes.description: Work examines perceived humanness, embodiment, interaction styles, social networks, and trust across diverse AI-enabled contexts.

themes.name: AI adoption, policy, and societal implications
themes.description: Analyses of adoption in organizations and education, governance frameworks, public-policy use of LLMs, and equity considerations.

emergingKeywords: governance and ethical oversight of AI
